title: Entering variations without the pieces

D0.outcome: Explains why the variation is entered in the head and checked on the board only at the end.

D1.outcome: Enters a six-ply variation without moving pieces, then states the position and the key threat in it, in at least 7 of 10 tests.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, finds a refutation 8 plies deep that needs a quiet move in the middle, with no board manipulation.

D3.outcome: Holds two branches of a tree at once and compares their end positions without writing them down.

misconceptions: Moving pieces on the board while thinking is the same skill.
Blind calculation needs a photographic memory.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S4 (Kotov, Aagaard, Ramesh, Dvoretsky, Rowson, Heisman, all [R] in the map) (CAL.BLIND T5-6)
conditions: The learner can already visualise five-ply lines reliably (CAL.VISUALIZE D3).
contrasts: The line is held until the first quiet move, then confused with an earlier position.
Holding too many branches and mixing their end positions.
A position that needs only a one-move check.
